clue.text: It may grow on the marsh's southern border

definitions.text: It may grow on the marsh's

parts.note: a border is an edge

explanation.surface: Something growing along the southern fringe of a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassy plant of wet ground, typical of bogs and fens.

clue.text: Remove from the register when the dispute is settled

explanation.surface: Deregistering someone at the end of a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: when a dispute is settled, the industrial action (the strike) is off.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete a name from an official roll, as with a struck-off doctor; and a strike being called off ends a dispute.

clue.text: Where to get meals on wheels

definitions.text: Where to get meals on wheels

parts.words: Where to get meals on wheels
parts.note: meals on wheels suggests a delivery service for the elderly, but read literally it is a place serving food aboard a moving train

explanation.surface: Asking where the meals-on-wheels service operates.
explanation.walkthrough: Meals on wheels is a British charity service bringing hot food to housebound people; here the wheels are a railway carriage's.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage fitted out as a restaurant, serving food while the train runs.

clue.text: One's distressed for ages

indicators.note: distressed means upset or knocked about, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has been upset for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges the four letters O, N, E, S of 'One's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are words for immensely long stretches of time.

clue.text: Attempt with unusual elation to be totally independent

parts.note: to have a go is to attempt

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of elation are put in an uncommon arrangement

explanation.surface: Trying something with uncharacteristic joy in order to be self-reliant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attempt' reads as the verb opening a sentence, but it supplies the noun 'go'; 'unusual' signals the shuffle of 'elation'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for acting alone, without help or partners.

clue.text: Made a subaltern infuriated

explanation.surface: An officer being promoted and losing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: A pip is the star worn on the shoulder by a British second lieutenant (a subaltern); 'the pip' is also British slang for irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Awarding someone a rank star promotes them to junior officer; giving someone the pip means annoying them intensely.

clue.text: Visionary conceives first-class train network

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A dreamer imagines a top-quality rail system.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) gives AI with the digit read as I; 'conceives' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy schemes are fanciful and unrealistic, like a dreamer's ideas.

clue.text: Unit going to Australia needs gas

indicators.note: going to tells us the unit travels to sit beside the word for Australia, after it

parts.note: Oz is a familiar name for Australia
a unit is the number one

explanation.surface: A unit posted to Australia requires fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' reads as travel to Australia; here it just says the unit is joined on after the familiar name for the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of oxygen, a pale blue gas found in the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Attempt prose composition

explanation.surface: Having a go at writing a piece of prose.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is a try at something, and also a short written piece on a subject.

clue.text: Confrontation results in arrest

explanation.surface: A clash ends with someone being taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is a quarrel or clash; to run someone in is slang for taking them into custody.

clue.text: Second-hand debts acquired by a cleric

indicators.note: acquired by places the debts as something the clergyman picks up, attached after him

parts.note: a vicar is a parish clergyman
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: A clergyman picks up debts from someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Experienced through another person rather than directly, like secondhand thrills.

clue.text: A Wimbledon wash-out may invite trouble

explanation.surface: A rained-off tennis tournament could cause problems.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; a court disaster is a calamity on court, and to court disaster is to risk ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe on a tennis court, and to court something is to invite it, so inviting calamity.

clue.text: Understanding type

explanation.surface: A sympathetic sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind means sympathetic or considerate, and also a sort or category.

clue.text: Extra money is good in France and America

parts.note: bon is French for good
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Additional cash is welcome on both sides of the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment beyond what is usual, such as an annual extra in a pay packet.

clue.text: Portrait painter left cathedral city

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: An artist has moved away from a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Peter Lely was the leading portraitist at the court of Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: Lely was a Dutch-born court artist famed for his likenesses of English royalty and nobles.

clue.text: Contemptuous expression always applied to Poles

indicators.note: applied to puts the word for always beside the poles, after them

parts.note: the two poles are south and north, S and N
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Permanent disdain is aimed at Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland, but it means the magnetic poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A scornful curl of the lip, a look of disdain.

clue.text: Bloomer is evident within twenty-four hours

indicators.note: within puts the word is inside the word for a day

parts.note: a day lasts twenty-four hours

explanation.surface: A mistake becomes obvious inside a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder or loaf, but here it is literally something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant is something that blooms, and this is a common white flower.

clue.text: To study US currency allocation requires prolonger thought

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
a cent is an American coin
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: Examining how American money is shared out takes deep thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustained mental focus on a single matter.

clue.text: With determination I get close to home

parts.note: near means close
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone gets close to their house with resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something seriously and wholeheartedly, with full resolve.

clue.text: Yours truly is top of the pops

explanation.surface: Writer claims to have the chart-topping record.
explanation.walkthrough: Number one is slang for oneself (look after number one), and the best-selling record in the pop charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Yours truly means oneself, and the chart-topping single holds the first spot.

clue.text: Insist on a decision to compel public flotation

explanation.surface: Demanding a resolution by forcing shares onto the market.
explanation.walkthrough: An issue of shares is a company's offer of stock to the public, so forcing the issue literally compels that offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To push matters to a resolution; also, literally, to oblige a share issue to go ahead.

clue.text: Much-applauded records made by batsmen

explanation.surface: Popular recordings produced by cricketers.
explanation.walkthrough: Batsmen are cricket players who strike the ball with the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Successful pop singles are popular songs; batsmen strike the ball, scoring strokes.

clue.text: What the woodcutter did when the lady accepted his proposal

definitions.text: when the lady accepted his proposal

explanation.surface: A woodsman's story of chopping trees and getting married.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words: when she accepted, he married her.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodcutter chopped timber, and after an accepted marriage proposal the man got married.

clue.text: In Islington I could get shot in the arm

indicators.note: In tells us the letters sit inside the run of words Islington I could

explanation.surface: Someone could be given an injection in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Islington is a district of north London; 'shot in the arm' looks like an injection but means a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that revives or invigorates, a restorative boost.

clue.text: His wife would eat only fat fish

definitions.text: His wife would eat only fat

explanation.surface: A man's wife has a peculiar diet of only fatty fish.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme, Jack Sprat could eat no fat and his wife could eat no lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack in the nursery rhyme bears this surname, which is also a small herring-like sea creature.

clue.text: life is only love, love only bliss."

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads only 'life is only love, love only bliss."' with an opening quotation and any definition missing; no wordplay can be parsed from it.
annotationWithheld.clue: life is only love, love only bliss."

clue.text: Jug in which to mix the ingredients

definitions.text: in which to mix the ingredients

explanation.surface: A pitcher used for blending recipe components.
explanation.walkthrough: Jug and stir are both slang for prison; the second definition means to mix by stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for prison; and to mix ingredients is to agitate them with a spoon.

clue.text: Examine a small container

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a can is a metal container

explanation.surface: Inspecting a little tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To look over carefully, scrutinise.

clue.text: The snooker player did when his nerve cracked?

definitions.text: The snooker player did when his nerve cracked?

parts.words: The snooker player did when his nerve cracked?
parts.note: a snooker player aims at a pocket, but the phrase for losing composure is also read as heading for the pocket

explanation.surface: A snooker player loses his nerve during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker a pot is sinking a ball; the idiom means deteriorated or fell apart.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for deteriorating badly or falling to pieces.

clue.text: Belief in sacred oratories

indicators.note: in shows the letters are found inside the words sacred oratories

explanation.surface: Faith expressed in religious choral works.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement of faith or principles, from the Latin for I believe.

clue.text: He smartens up the house for an Advent preacher

parts.note: Advent falls in December, abbreviated Dec
an orator is a public speaker, as a preacher is

explanation.surface: A man spruces up his house ready for a preacher arriving in Advent.
explanation.walkthrough: Advent is the church season of the four weeks before Christmas, so it stands for its month.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter and paperhanger who improves the look of homes.

clue.text: Inert mixture added to gunpowder

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun: something that is added to gunpowder

indicators.note: mixture says the letters of inert are mixed up

explanation.surface: An unreactive blend is put into explosive powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' rearranges INERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a main ingredient of black powder explosive.
